notes: HQ36, Vico's new story (2026-11-05): digital, drafting, oil painting. 22.5 s (+4.5). Opens on the studio's painting easel, still life and cast bust in the window light, glides past them and settles on the desk: flat at 0 deg with a pen display (digital), lifts to 52 in (blue; keeps the stool clearance), tilts 0->40 deg (purple): at 9 deg the pen display is put away and the drafting kit + easel rail appear, the painter's side shelf pops in at ~28 deg; then 40->55 deg (purple): the app's auto-stow swaps to the artist easel and painting at 50 deg, shelf stays. Camera rests through each 1.25 s white pause and ends on a slow push on the painting, stool and palette in front. Needs film-fx accessories.add[].visible (timed visibility). Keyboard tray, keyboard, mouse and the small pen tablet are off this desk. Ch3 easel fix (Vico, 2026-11-06: 'the painting graphic itself needs to be also rotated 180, just the graphic' / 'the easel bar for the drafting items are still there'): the drafting act's items (drafting kit with the wireframe plan, and the easel rail = the drafting bar across the board's front edge) fade out 16.9-18.7 s and are held hidden from 18.8 s; the artist easel (placement unchanged, rotation 180) fades in 17.5-19.3 s and only its painting texture is turned 180 deg (film-edits material.mapRotation). Timing used to hand the rail and kit back to the app (visible null), which kept the rail. Digital->drafting hand-off (Vico's 16:09 cut starts the drafting tilt at 6.8 s; the app stows the pen display at 9 deg, ~7.65 s): pen display fades out 7.0-7.4 s (held hidden from 7.4), drafting kit + rail fade in 7.0-7.4 s (shown from 7.0), so the board is never empty (was: kit at 10.78 s). Second pass (Vico 16:19, after the stills: 'the easel bar should be on the bottom of the painting, and it also needs to be rotated 180' / 'the easel bar [drafting] needs to also be flipped 180, it's upside down' / 'the oil painting one needs to be the same location after you flip it'): the easel rail (drafting bar) is rolled 180 so its lip holds the paper on the board's front edge; the artist easel goes back to rotation 0 so its ledge sits at the bottom of the painting, on the rail's own spot, and the painting reads upright with no texture turn (mapRotation 0 replaces the earlier 180).
